sections.h2: Which Houston County office handles my property tax question?
sections.html:
Three groups share the job here: the Tax Commissioner, the Tax Assessors and the three city offices. Collections happen at a Warner Robins office and a Perry office. Valuation and homestead filings happen in Perry. The assessors' own FAQ says they never send out bills.

Both commissioner offices open weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. The county's pay-and-search portal lets you look up taxes online and adds a convenience fee to each payment.

sections.h2: How did Houston County grow into the Robins Air Force Base area?
sections.html:
The county dates to May 15, 1821 and carries the name of Governor John Houstoun, minus the letter u. Wattsville became the seat because it lay in the middle of the new county. It was incorporated as Perry by 1824, and the county's statistics page calls Perry the geographic center of Georgia. Two national highways later crossed in town, which earned it the name Crossroads of Georgia. Peach orchards made the county famous by 1870.

Warner Robins began as a depot the Army Corps of Engineers built on cotton fields near Wellston during World War II, and it incorporated on March 5, 1943. Centerville incorporated in 1958 and takes its name from lying between Macon and Perry. Interstate 75 and the first hospital arrived in the 1960s. The county history now calls Robins Air Force Base Houston County's biggest employer and the fourth biggest in Georgia.

  • Area: 375.54 square miles, 67th largest among Georgia's 159 counties.
  • Roads: 1,088.2 miles, 94.5% of them paved.
  • Cities: Centerville, Perry and Warner Robins.
  • Fairgrounds: the Georgia National Fairgrounds & Agricenter opened in 1990.

sections.h2: What do Houston County housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
QuickFacts puts Houston at 178,214 people in July 2025, an 8.9% rise over the April 2020 base. The county holds 74,635 housing units and permitted 1,218 more in 2025. Workers travel 22.8 minutes on average, a shorter trip than Heard's 34.9 or Henry's 33.1.

  • Typical owner-occupied house: $219,800.
  • Homeowners occupy 66.9% of housing, so roughly a third of households rent.
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,208.
  • Typical household income: $80,698.
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or more: 32.5%.

Sellers who rented a house out before listing it should check whether the homestead exemption still applies, because the county describes the exemption as applying to property the taxpayer owns and occupies as a legal residence.

sections.h2: Who is buying and selling homes in Houston County?
sections.html:
Employment data points to a steady local job base. QuickFacts lists 2,832 employer establishments in 2023 with 44,134 jobs, a 5.1% rise from 2022, and annual payroll near $1.86 billion. Health care and social assistance receipts reached about $879 million in 2022, and retail sales ran $18,898 per resident. The county also counts 19,366 veterans for 2020 to 2024.

The county's statistics page says the county had 105,808 residents in 1998, and that twenty-three public schools have earned the Georgia School of Excellence label and four have been named National Blue Ribbon Schools. Sellers in Perry, Warner Robins and Centerville can expect buyers to weigh school and base-commute information alongside price.

sections.h2: How does Houston County set the value my tax is based on?
sections.html:
On the Tax Commissioner's page, fair market value is pinned to January 1 and the taxable amount is assessed value, set by law at 40% of it. A mill is $1.00 for every $1,000 of assessed value. Whenever the Board of Tax Assessors alters a value from last year, or from the figure an owner returned, it must mail a notice.

Real property returns on form PT-50R, plus applications for conservation use, exempt status and similar programs, must be mailed with a US postmark on or before April 1. Personal property returns share that date and are taken by mail only, with forms sent in January to anyone who owns a boat, an aircraft or a business. Call (478) 218-4750 about real estate. Parcel records are searchable on the county's qpublic site.

A seller wondering whether a city levy was paid must call Warner Robins, Perry or Centerville directly, since the assessors do not bill. Confirmation of county and school tax comes from the commissioner.

sections.h2: How do I claim a Houston County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Submit your first application to the Tax Assessor's Office before April 1 of the year the benefit should start. Approved exemptions roll over annually. You file again only when ownership changes or you want a different exemption.

The statewide standard exemption removes $2,000 from assessed value, per the state revenue department, and some counties layer larger local exemptions on top. Ask the assessors at (478) 218-4750 which amounts apply to your parcel, and have a mid-year buyer ask how the closing date affects first-year eligibility.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Houston County valuation?
sections.html:
Your clock is 45 days from the mailing date on the notice. The Board of Tax Assessors hears it first, re-examines its number and writes back. Unresolved appeals continue to the County Board of Equalization for a scheduled hearing and a ruling at its close. Superior court comes after that, and the county says arbitration can replace the Board of Equalization step.

  • Permitted grounds: whether the property is taxable, the value assigned, or uniformity against similar properties.
  • Excluded: any gripe about the tax rate or amount levied.
  • Hearing officer option: limited to non-homestead real estate over $500,000.
  • Arbitration option: value only, with a certified appraisal.

If a board rules against you, a written notice of superior court appeal is due in 30 days under the state's summary, and unpaid prior-year tax blocks the hearing. Email property tax questions to taxquestions@houstoncountyga.gov.

sections.h2: What are the Houston County tax due dates, and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
Houston's commissioner pages list no fixed due date, so go by your bill or phone (478) 542-2110. The statewide default is December 20, which a county may shift to December 1 or November 15 or replace with installments. Interest waits until 60 days after the bill is postmarked.

Title on January 1 decides who owes, and a seller leaving partway through the year gets no refund under state rules. For a Perry or Warner Robins sale, have the closing agent list county, school and city taxes on separate lines, because the cities send their own bills.

An unpaid bill can lead to a recorded lien and a later auction. Afterward, Georgia's Consumer Ed office says, a twelve-month window lets interested parties redeem by paying the bid, subsequent taxes, special assessments and a 20% premium.

faqs.q: Does the Houston County Tax Assessor mail my bill?
faqs.a: No, because the assessors' FAQ says the office does not handle billing. Phone the commissioner at (478) 542-2110 (Warner Robins) or (478) 218-4940 (Perry) for county bills, and call your city for a city levy.

faqs.q: By when must I file a Houston County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The cutoff is April 1 of the first year you want the benefit, and the paperwork goes to the assessors. Once approved it carries forward without a new form, until the home changes hands or you ask for a different exemption.

faqs.q: How many days do I get to appeal in Houston County?
faqs.a: The window is 45 days from the day the notice was mailed, and the assessors receive the filing first. Arguing that the tax is simply too high is off the table, while taxability, value and uniformity are fair game.

faqs.q: Where can I visit the Houston County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: The Warner Robins office is on Carl Vinson Parkway (number 202), and the Perry office is on Perry Parkway (number 201). Counters stay open every weekday from half past eight until five.

faqs.q: Who pays Houston County tax when a house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable for the full year, and no partial-year refund exists. Ask the closing agent to break out county, school and city lines.
